item.title: Version 3.0.8
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.8

  • Remio Host keeps itself up to date — New versions now download in the background and install on their own while no device is connected, so a Mac you reach from far away stays current without anyone sitting at it. Turn it off any time in Settings → Install updates automatically.
  • A required update no longer takes your Mac offline — When an update was required, the Host stopped sharing until it was installed, and on many Macs it waited for someone to click a button on the Mac itself. It now keeps sharing and installs the update at the next quiet moment.
  • Fixed "it says it updated, then asks to update again" — If you installed a new version from the website while Remio Host was running, the Host kept running the old version and kept asking for the update. It now switches to the new version by itself.
  • A MacBook with its lid closed shows the picture — A MacBook on power with its lid closed could accept your connection and then show nothing. It now wakes itself up for you and streams.
  • A lid-closed MacBook keeps its external display — With the lid closed and one external display attached, every other session could leave that display switched off afterwards, and the Mac would go to sleep. Your display now comes back exactly as it was.

item.title: Version 3.0.7
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.7

Bug Fixes

  • Connecting from a phone or tablet no longer ends in "reopen Remio" — On some Macs, the display the Host creates for your phone or tablet didn't come up, and the Host took that for a missing permission: it stopped sharing and told you to reopen Remio, even while another device was streaming from the same Mac without trouble. It now tries that display again and, if it still doesn't appear, streams your Mac's own screen instead — sharing stays on.
  • Files you send to your Mac show up where you can see them — Since 3.0, a file the Host received only raised a notification, easy to miss when you're looking at the Mac through Remio. The Host now shows the file in a Finder window on the screen you're viewing, as it did before 3.0.

Improvements

  • A sharper picture on 120 Hz screens when your Mac is at its limit — When your Mac couldn't keep up with a large 120 Hz screen, such as an iPad Pro 13", the Host kept 120 fps and lowered the resolution, so text looked soft. It now steps down to 60 fps first — still smooth — and lowers the resolution only if 60 fps is too much as well. Over a relay connection a Mac at its limit now holds 60 fps too, instead of letting the frame rate fall.

item.title: Version 3.0.6
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.6

Bug Fixes

  • Detailed scenes no longer freeze the picture — Opening a large photo or cutting to a busy new scene at high resolution could freeze the stream for about three seconds, with nothing to say why. Every frame the Host sends now arrives in one piece, so the picture keeps moving.
  • Text-heavy screens keep their full frame rate — On a large screen full of text, the stream could quietly settle at half its frame rate. It now holds the full rate.
  • The Host picks itself up if the Mac's video encoder hangs — Rarely, macOS's video encoder stops answering. The Host then still showed as online, but no device could connect, sometimes for hours. It now notices within seconds and restarts itself.
  • No more unexpected restarts — The Host could restart itself every few minutes in three cases: on a Mac mini after a session ended, while the "You're up to date" message was left on screen, and while macOS was waiting for permission to use the Host's saved key. None of these restart it any more.

Improvements

  • Full sharpness at 120 Hz on big screens — On large, high-refresh sessions the Host used to lower the resolution and fall back to 60 fps to keep up. It now keeps full resolution at 120 fps, and returns to full sharpness sooner after a busy moment.
  • 120 Hz sessions start at full quality — A 120 Hz session on your local network started at half the quality your connection could carry, and was capped below the limit you set. It now starts at the right quality and uses your limit.

item.title: Version 3.0.5
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.5

Bug Fixes

  • Fast motion no longer falls behind — Scrolling a long page, playing a video or anything else that changes the whole screen could leave the picture, and every click and keystroke with it, more than a second behind on a local network. The Host now sends each frame as soon as it is ready, so what you do shows up right away — even at 120 Hz.
  • The Host uses your cable again — On a Mac connected by both a cable and Wi‑Fi, the stream could run over Wi‑Fi. It now picks the wired connection, for a steadier picture with less delay.

item.title: Version 3.0.4
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.4

Bug Fixes

  • Turning on screen sharing is noticed straight away — A Mac where you had switched Remio Host on under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Remote Desktop could stay on "Waiting for you" for good, however many times you pressed Recheck, reopened Remio or reinstalled it. The Host now sees the switch within seconds, and a Mac that was stuck this way starts sharing as soon as it updates — nothing to grant again.
  • No more detour to the wrong settings page — Right after the first permission prompt, macOS could show a second one whose button opened Screen & System Audio Recording instead of Remote Desktop. That second prompt no longer appears, and every button in Remio takes you straight to Remote Desktop. If you already turned Remio Host on under Screen & System Audio Recording, that works too — leave it as it is.

Improvements

  • A Mac you leave on stays reachable — If the Host ever crashes or freezes while you're away, it now starts again by itself: within seconds after a crash, a little over a minute after a freeze. Quitting Remio yourself still quits it. The helper that does this shows up as a background item from Remio Host in System Settings → General → Login Items; switching it off there turns it off.
  • Back online by itself after long sleeps — After the Mac had been asleep for more than an hour, or its clock had drifted, the Host could be turned away by the connection server and stay offline until someone restarted it. It now reconnects on its own, and keeps retrying while the network is down instead of waiting for a change it might never notice.
  • Screen sharing keeps coming back — When macOS cuts the screen capture and the first retries fail, the Host now keeps trying every ten minutes for as long as it takes, instead of giving up and waiting for someone at the Mac.

item.title: Version 3.0.3
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.3

  • The Host window's sidebar is back on macOS Sequoia — on macOS 15 the sidebar opened with its rows pushed up under the window buttons and the rest of the column empty, so there was no way to reach Connect, File sharing, Accessories, Devices or Permissions. The full list of pages is back.
  • A display set to "Fit to this device" now actually follows it — switching a virtual display to follow the device viewing it could come back refused, leaving it at the fixed size it already had.

item.title: Version 3.0.2
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.2

Bug Fixes

  • A Mac that stopped sharing because the screen capture broke now starts sharing again on its own — If macOS cut the capture mid-session and the automatic retries could not bring it back, the Host used to switch sharing off and wait for someone to press Start on the Mac. It now comes back by itself after a few seconds (waiting longer if it keeps happening), and only asks for a hand when the capture is genuinely broken.
  • Devices no longer see the Mac as online when it has stopped sharing — After that kind of stop, the Host kept telling the server it still had its old room, so every device saw the Mac online, and every connect failed with "no active host" until the Host was restarted. The Host now drops the room the moment it stops, and corrects itself if the server ever reports the room gone while it is idle.
  • The Host window is dark on every Mac, whatever the Mac itself is set to — On a Mac set to Light appearance the window's own frame stayed light around a dark page: the sidebar came up pale with white text on it, and a grey band sat across the top of the window. The sidebar, the title bar and every sheet and alert are now dark, the way the rest of the app already was.
  • A Mac that once took a required update is offered ordinary updates again — After a required update had installed itself, the Host went on quietly downloading later releases in the background instead of telling you about them — and since a Mac you leave on is rarely quit, those releases never finished installing. It asks again before installing, and now looks for a new version every hour.

item.title: Version 3.0.1
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.1

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed the Host window on macOS Sequoia — On macOS 15 the sidebar opened with a single row tucked under the window buttons and the rest of the column empty, so there was no way to reach Connect, File sharing, Accessories, Devices or Permissions. The full list of pages is back, and the window now opens the same way on every version of macOS.

item.title: Version 3.0.0
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.0

New Features

  • A new Host window — Remio Host now looks and behaves like System Settings: a sidebar with Connect, File sharing, Accessories, Devices, Permissions and Settings, and a real screen behind each one. Everything used to be floating panels stacked over a QR code, appearing and disappearing on their own; now each thing has a place you can go back to. The window also keeps the height you drag it to.
  • Send and receive files — The File sharing page sends files to the device you're connected from and receives files sent back the other way. Every transfer keeps a line in the history under the name of the device it came from or went to, so you can open a file you were sent last week in Finder, or send the same file again to the same device with one click.
  • A file arriving while your Mac is locked waits for you — If your Mac locks in the middle of an incoming file, the transfer pauses with a countdown instead of quietly writing to your disk while nobody is at the keyboard, and picks up exactly where it left off when you unlock.
  • A Devices page that tells you where access came from — Your devices are now grouped by how they got in: paired with a code on this Mac, or trusted because they're signed in to your account. Open any of them to see what it actually is — model, system, app version, screen, how it connects — give it a name of your own, or take its access away.
  • Two different ways to take access away — Block from this Mac keeps the device on your account but stops it reaching this computer. Remove from account signs it out everywhere. The buttons now say which one you're about to do, instead of one Remove that quietly did more than it looked like.
  • A log of what happened with your devices — The last 30 days of pairings, refused attempts, wrong PINs, session takeovers and revocations, in plain language, per device and across the Mac. A badge appears on Devices when something worth looking at happened while you weren't watching.
  • A Permissions page that's always there — Permissions used to be a panel that only appeared when something was broken, which is exactly when it's too late to find it. It's now a permanent place in the sidebar showing what each permission is for and what state it's in. When a macOS update quietly stops a permission from working, the page says so and tells you to switch it off and back on — rather than sending you to press Allow on something that's already allowed. Granting a permission in System Settings is noticed within seconds; you don't have to restart Remio or come back to the window.
  • Your pairing code expires — The six-digit code now lasts five minutes, with the countdown on screen, and rotates itself. Five wrong attempts replace it immediately and tell you it happened. A code left on screen all afternoon was a code anyone on the network could keep guessing at.
  • Choose whether your own devices skip pairing — Settings has a switch for letting devices signed in to your account connect without a code. On by default.

Improvements

  • Connecting is quicker — Setting up the display on the way into a session dropped from 1.69 to 0.76 seconds, which is time your device spends on "Connecting…" before the first frame.
  • The session panel says what the connection is actually doing — Packet loss, jitter and how many times the picture froze now sit alongside bitrate and latency, so a session that feels wrong can be pointed at something.
  • When a second device takes over, the window says so — Handing a session to another device now names the device that took it, marks it as the new owner and restarts the session clock, instead of silently swapping who is in control.
  • Disconnecting a device no longer looks like unpairing it — Pressing Disconnect told the device it was "no longer paired", which made it look like it had lost access for good. It now says this Mac ended the session, and the device can simply connect again.
  • One name for each permission, on every screen — "Screen sharing" and "Mouse and keyboard control" are called that everywhere in Remio. Apple's own names appear only inside the step-by-step instructions, word for word as macOS writes them, so what you read here matches what you're looking for over there.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a Mac with both Ethernet and Wi‑Fi on hosting over Wi‑Fi — When a cable and Wi‑Fi were both connected, the host could offer its Wi‑Fi address first and every client would stream through it. The wired connection now takes precedence.
  • Fixed your monitors coming back in the wrong order — A display arranged to the left of your main one came back on the right after a session, and any vertical offset was lost, leaving your mouse crossing between screens in the wrong direction until you fixed it by hand. Remio now records where every display actually sits and puts them back exactly.
  • Fixed a left click opening the right-click menu — After using any shortcut with Control, every click that followed behaved as a Control-click for the rest of the session, so left-clicking opened context menus.
  • Fixed copying on your device and pasting on the Mac giving you the old text — Copying something on the device you're controlling from and pressing ⌘V on the Mac could paste the previous thing, or nothing at all, and the workaround was pasting into another app and copying again. Every copy now lands. Your Mac's clipboard is also no longer replaced by the device's the moment you connect.
  • Fixed the Host freezing seconds after a device connects — On a Mac signed in to the same iCloud account as another Apple device, something copied on that other device could stop the Host dead as it tried to fetch the content over the network.
  • Fixed the Host quitting when a device offered an impossible file — A single message claiming a file size that couldn't exist took the whole Host down, session included. Oversized files are refused with a message now.
  • Fixed the window getting shorter every time you opened it — The window lost about fifty points of height per launch — 658, then 606, then 554 — and forgot whatever height you had set for it.
  • Fixed reconnecting from the same device resetting the session clock — A brief network drop restarted the timer as if a new device had arrived, and numbers from the previous connection could be shown under the new device's name.
  • Fixed a failed transfer you couldn't do anything about — A transfer that failed left a row in the history with no way to retry it or pick a different file.
  • Fixed small files showing as "0 KB" — Anything under a kilobyte reported itself as empty while it transferred perfectly well.
